prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 – summary (≤500 words)

Core vision
- Stop Brexit to protect prosperity, rights and the Union; use a £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in services and cut inequality.
- Put wellbeing, climate action and equality at the heart of government.

Economy and work
- Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing) and £5bn to relaunch a Green Investment Bank.
- UK2050 innovation plan: raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapults; regionalise research funding; support creative and digital sectors.
- Skills Wallet: £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning; expand apprenticeships via a broader Skills & Training Levy.
- Fair taxes: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tougher action on avoidance, especially tech giants; scrap Marriage Tax Allowance.
- Workers’ rights: day‑one flexible working; new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; 20% higher minimum wage for zero‑hours in normal demand; right to request fixed hours; stronger enforcement.

Education and childcare
- Free, high‑quality childcare from nine months for working parents (35 hours, 48 weeks); extend to all 2–4‑year‑olds; £1bn for Children’s Centres; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; clear repairs backlog; fix SEND funding.
- Scrap SATs and league tables; replace Ofsted; introduce a broad “curriculum for life”; protect arts.
- FE: +£1bn; restore maintenance grants; student mental health charter.

Climate, nature and transport
- Net zero by 2045; at least 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; permanent fracking ban.
- Ten‑year plan to insulate homes and end fuel poverty by 2025; zero‑carbon new homes from 2021 (rising to Passivhaus by 2025).
- Circular economy law: ban non‑recyclable single‑use plastics within three years; 70% recycling target; deposit return schemes.
- Nature: Nature Act with binding targets; plant 60m trees a year; restore peat/wetlands; protect 50% of UK waters.
- Transport: all new cars/vans electric by 2030; Clean Air Act; extend ULEZ to 10 more cities; £4.5bn for buses; cycling/walking to 10% of transport budget; rail fares freeze; reopen lines/stations; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; back HS2/NPR with tighter controls.

Health and social care
- 1p on Income Tax raising £7bn/yr ringfenced for NHS and social care; £10bn capital fund. Long‑term: explore a dedicated Health & Care Tax; integrate NHS, social care and public health.
- Mental health parity: new waiting‑time standards; big expansion of talking therapies; 24/7 crisis care; perinatal support; implement Mental Health Act reforms.
- End GP shortfall by 2025; national workforce strategy; better support for carers, including guaranteed respite.

Fair society, housing and justice
- Fix Universal Credit: first payment in five days; scrap two‑child limit and benefits cap; right to food; end sanctions regime; raise Local Housing Allowance; abolish bedroom tax.
- Build 300,000 homes a year including 100,000 for social rent; zero‑carbon standards; Rent to Own; longer tenancies; mandatory landlord licensing; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Policing and crime: £1bn for community policing; £500m for youth services; public‑health approach to violence; Online Crime Agency; presumption against short prison sentences; focus on rehabilitation; tackle BAME disparities.

Rights, equality, immigration and asylum
- Defend Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore Legal Aid; halt police facial recognition; no‑fault divorce; complete equal marriage reforms.
- Tackle hate crime; modernise Gender Recognition; X‑gender passports; end period poverty; stronger diversity and pay‑gap reporting; six weeks’ paternity leave.
- Immigration: end hostile environment; 28‑day detention limit; move visa policy out of Home Office; keep EU freedom of movement; fair family rules; two‑year post‑study work; cut child citizenship fees.
- Asylum: right to work after three months; resettle 10,000 refugees and 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years; faster, fairer decisions.

Democracy and devolution
- Proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; votes for long‑term EU residents and UK citizens abroad; reform Lords; citizens’ assemblies; a federal UK with a written constitution and deeper devolution.

Global affairs
- Champion multilateralism; 0.7% aid; suspend arms sales to Saudi Arabia; NATO 2% defence, cyber investment, minimal nuclear deterrent; recognise Palestine; support Hong Kong BNOs; lead global climate action (Paris, plastics treaty, biodiversity, end fossil subsidies).
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Conservative', 'Labour', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Scottish National Party', 'Green Party']
}
